# **Bland AI Alternatives in 2026: What I'd Pick If You're Not an Enterprise**

Meta title: Bland AI Alternatives (2026): Picks for Small Businesses. 

Meta description: Bland keeps warm transfer and texting on Enterprise. Compare six alternatives on features by plan, real cost per minute, and setup effort.

If you signed up for Bland to answer and book calls, you’ve probably found that the features a front desk needs aren’t on the plan you bought. Bland’s docs put warm transfer, where the AI briefs your staff before connecting the caller, and texting on its Enterprise or limited Agent Phone plan. Its pricing page lists a BAA for Enterprise only.

Here is how I sort the options. A small business with no developer that wants live transfer, booking and per-minute pricing should start with Botphonic. A practice that needs a BAA on its entry plan today should look at My AI Front Desk. If most of your callers are repeat callers, Goodcall’s per-caller pricing may suit you best. With a developer, Retell or Vapi give you more control, and ElevenLabs Agents fit when voice quality and languages come first. A regulated enterprise handling calls at volume is better off staying on Bland Enterprise.

I went through each tool’s pricing page, documentation and public demo, and I say where I also tried a tool myself. Below you’ll see what Bland’s plans include, what each option costs at your volume, and what moving takes.

## **The Options at a Glance**

A BAA is the HIPAA agreement a clinic needs before a vendor handles patient information. If you don’t handle patient health information, you can ignore that part.

| Tool | Best for | Starting price |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Botphonic | Small businesses with no developer that want live transfer and booking | \$0.13 a minute pay-as-you-go, or from \$12 a month billed yearly |
| My AI Front Desk | Practices that need a BAA on the entry plan | \$79 a month billed yearly, or \$99 a month |
| Goodcall | Businesses with mostly repeat callers | \$79 a month for 100 unique customers |
| Retell AI | Teams with a developer | \$0.07 to \$0.31 a minute, built from parts |
| Vapi | Developers and agencies | \$0.05 a minute for hosting, plus provider costs |
| ElevenLabs Agents | Voice quality and many languages | Free for 15 minutes, then from \$6 a month |

## **What Bland's Self-Serve Plans Include**

I’ll start with what Bland does well. Its per-minute rate includes the AI model, transcription and premium voices, so there are no separate token charges. The voices in its demo are good too. For a team with engineers, that is a real advantage.

Bland’s pricing page shows Start at \$0 a month and \$0.14 a minute, and Build at \$299 a month and \$0.12 a minute. Its billing docs also list a Scale plan at \$499 a month and \$0.11 a minute, which the pricing page doesn’t show. Start allows 10 calls at once and 100 calls a day, while Build allows 50 and 2,000.

Now the part that matters for a small office: what those plans leave out. Bland’s warm transfer doc says Start and Build get cold transfer, where the call connects with no introduction. Warm transfer is limited to Enterprise and a separate Agent Phone plan. Its SMS doc limits texting the same way, and its pricing page lists a BAA for Enterprise only. Booking is built in only through Cal.com, using an access key.

The Agent Phone plan costs \$29.99 a month and covers one agent number with unlimited US and Canada minutes. But it handles one call at a time and 50 calls a day. That makes it a different product from the one a busy office would run on.

Some costs also come on top of the headline rate. Transfer time costs \$0.05 a minute on Start and \$0.04 on Build when you use Bland's numbers, and nothing if you bring your own Twilio number. Outbound call attempts cost \$0.015 each on Bland's phone service, and number fees and phone service add more. I go through the plans in more detail in [Bland's pricing, plan by plan](https://botphonic.ai/blog/bland-ai-pricing/).

Bland did not get worse. It chose a different kind of customer, and a ten-person office is probably not that customer.

## **How I Chose These**

I compared each option on five questions that a business owner would ask:

1. Are the front-desk features (transfer, texting, booking) on the plan I would actually buy?  
2. What will I pay at my call volume, all in?  
3. Can I set it up without a developer?  
4. Can I build it myself if I want control?  
5. Can I use it for patient calls?

Everything here comes from each company’s own pricing page, documentation, and public demo, checked between October 26 and 29, 2026\. I left out phone systems and contact-center suites, since a small office is not replacing those. My full write-up of Bland is in my [Bland AI review](https://botphonic.ai/blog/bland-ai-review/).

## **Bland AI Alternatives Compared: Features, Cost, and Setup**

| Tool | Transfer to your staff | Texting or confirmation | Booking calendar | BAA |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Bland AI | Cold on Start and Build; warm on Enterprise or Agent Phone | Enterprise or Agent Phone | Cal.com | Enterprise only |
| Botphonic | Live transfer (warm) | A confirmation after booking via email | Calendly, Cal.com and Google Calendar | Signs a BAA |
| My AI Front Desk | Hot transfer with backup numbers | SMS reminders | Google Calendar | On every plan |
| Goodcall | Tries up to three people | Texts the owner; no caller confirmation described | Google Calendar | Its pages disagree; confirm in writing |

*“Hot transfer” means the AI connects the caller to a live person right away. Retell’s “agentic warm transfer” is its AI-assisted version of warm transfer. Texting from a US business number usually needs carrier registration (A2P), which is the extra setup mentioned above.*

Read the table against your own must-haves. Say you need a person to receive transferred calls, a confirmation for the caller, a BAA and no code. Any tool that meets all four without extra setup or an enterprise contract is a candidate. Then use the cost table to see how each bills at your volume.

## **The Six Alternatives, and Who Each One Is For**

I have ordered these by how much setup each asks of you. The first three are built for people who do not write code. The last three assume someone on your side does.

### **1\. Botphonic**

![][image1]

**Why I included it:** Live transfer, booking during the call and a confirmation are the front-desk features Bland keeps on Enterprise. Botphonic offers them on its self-serve plans.

**Best for:** A small business that wants calls answered, booked and handed to a person without a developer or an enterprise contract.

**Price:**

* **Pay-as-you-go:** Starter is \$0.13 a minute with a \$75 wallet. Pro is \$0.12 a minute with a \$125 wallet. Credit doesn’t expire.  
* **Monthly plans:** Starter is \$15 a month, or \$12 billed yearly, for 100 minutes and 5 calls at once. Pro is \$45 a month, or \$36 billed yearly, for 300 minutes and 10 calls at once.  
* **Extras:** Phone numbers are \$1.48 a month.  
* **Trial:** 14 days with 20 free minutes, after a \$1 card check.

**My take:** I think Botphonic suits a business that wants to transfer to its own staff, book during the call and send the caller a confirmation without writing code. It also fits a business that would rather pay by the minute than by unique caller or in a fixed bundle.

I listened to the six sample calls on the homepage, including a healthcare receptionist and appointment booking. I also tried the demo and had an agent built within minutes. The visual workflow builder is drag-and-drop, and the team can set it up for you if you’d rather not. It lists HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Zapier, Google Calendar, Cal.com and Calendly as integrations. It signs a BAA, which matters if you handle patient calls.

![][image2]

### **2\. My AI Front Desk**

![][image3]

**Why I included it:** It’s the most complete package here for small practices, with a BAA on every plan. Bland keeps that on Enterprise.

**Best for:** A small clinic or service business that needs a BAA and wants calls, texts and web chat on one plan.

**Skip it if:** You expect to pass about 1,000 minutes a month, or you want a refund option, since its terms say fees are non-refundable.

**Price:** \$99 a month, or \$79 billed yearly, with 200 voice minutes and \$0.25 a minute after that. Its HIPAA page says \$109 a month flat, which conflicts with the pricing page, so confirm before you sign up.

**My take:** Its setup guide puts everything on one Receptionist page with about 15 settings, followed by a test call. When I tested it, I was able to create and customize an AI voice receptionist. Its pages say it books into Google Calendar during the call with a double-booking guard and sends SMS reminders. I found the integration options harder to follow than the rest of the setup.

### **3\. Goodcall**

![][image4]

**Why I included it:** It’s built for owner-operators, the opposite of Bland’s move toward enterprises. Per-caller billing can beat any per-minute rate if your customers call repeatedly.

**Best for:** An owner-operated business whose calls come mostly from the same customers.

**Skip it if:** You get many one-time callers, or you need a BAA you can verify, since its own pages contradict each other.

**Price:** Starter is \$79 a month for 100 unique customers, then 79 cents each. Growth is \$129 for 500, then 26 cents each. Scale is \$299 for 2,000, then 15 cents each. Minutes aren’t metered, and Starter allows one external tool, one team member and 30 days of history.

**My take:** Signup starts by looking up your business on Google Maps, and setup is fast. In my testing it was voice-only, with no web chat or WhatsApp. It books into Google Calendar, texts the owner and transfers to up to three people. Keep an eye on the cap on new callers each month, since overage fees apply after it.

### **4\. Retell AI**

![][image5]

**Why I included it:** It offers warm transfer on pay-as-you-go.

**Best for:** A business with a developer or agency that wants Bland-style control without an enterprise contract.

**Skip it if:** Nobody on your team wants to own the instructions, integrations and text-message setup, or you want one flat price.

**Price:** Pay-as-you-go runs \$0.07 to \$0.31 a minute, built from \$0.055 for infrastructure plus the model, the voice, \$0.015 for phone service and any add-ons. New accounts get \$10 in credit and 20 calls at once. Numbers are \$2 a month, and texting is \$20 a month plus \$0.01 a message.

**My take:** Retell is the closest swap if you liked Bland’s control but not its Enterprise gate. I used the free \$10 credit to create a voice agent and make live calls. Signing up for a simple demo is easy, but moving on to logic and JSON routing gets complex for non-technical users. 

In my comparison, it also offered less local infrastructure and multi-language support than some other platforms. See my [Retell alternatives guide](https://botphonic.ai/blog/retell-ai-alternative/).

### **5\. Vapi**

### **![][image6]**

**Why I included it:** It’s the most developer-focused option here, for people who want to choose every part of the system.

**Best for:** Developers and agencies building custom agents.

**Skip it if:** You don’t have a developer, or you’re a practice that can’t justify \$2,000 a month for HIPAA.

**Price:** \$0.05 a minute for hosting, plus the transcriber, model and voice at provider cost. Vapi’s own estimate is \$82 to \$129 per 1,000 minutes. Support starts at \$29 a month, and the HIPAA add-on is \$2,000 a month.

**My take:** Vapi is for a developer, not a business owner, and its own pages say it’s built for builders. In my demo, credits went faster than I expected, because Vapi is an orchestration layer. You pay its \$0.05 a minute hosting fee plus separate usage costs for the speech-to-text, language model and text-to-speech providers you choose. Because calls hop across several outside services, I saw delays that ranged from under half a second to several seconds, and bills can be hard to predict. 

### **6\. ElevenLabs Agents**

![][image7]

**Why I included it:** If you chose Bland for how the voices sound, ElevenLabs is the voice company, and it now has a full agents platform with low entry prices.

**Best for:** Developers and enterprises that put voice quality and many languages first.

**Skip it if:** You want a done-for-you receptionist with Google Calendar booking and confirmation texts and don’t want to write instructions or tools, or you need a BAA below Enterprise.

**Price:** Free (15 minutes), Starter \$6 (75 minutes), Creator \$22 (275 minutes), Pro \$99 (1,238 minutes), Scale \$299 (3,738 minutes) and Business \$990 (12,375 minutes). Extra minutes are \$0.08. AI model usage is billed on top, phone service is billed by Twilio or your phone provider, and concurrent calls range from 4 to 40 by plan.

**My take:** I’d point this at a Bland user who has a developer, or a confident tinkerer, and cares most about the voice. Its docs show Cal.com as a native integration connected with an access key, but Google Calendar isn’t documented as native. 

Transfer to a number, voicemail detection, and language detection come built in. Its HIPAA page says a BAA is available only on Enterprise. I did not find a public demo call on its agents page.

## **Who Should Stay on Bland**

Bland is a serious product for the customers it’s built for. If you run regulated, high-stakes calls at volume and have engineers who want to build and test their own flows, Enterprise is designed for that. I wouldn’t move you away from it. The rest of this guide is for everyone else.

## **Moving From Bland**

This section applies mainly if you built agents on Bland’s older pathways. Bland’s migration doc set November 15, 2026 as the deadline for moving production agents to its new Agents setup, and said pathways still handling traffic afterward would be migrated for you. That date has now passed, so check the doc for the current status. If you built a simple receptionist on a self-serve plan, you may have little to migrate.

Either way, it’s a fair moment to decide whether to rebuild on Bland or move to something simpler. Keep Bland running until the new setup has handled real calls.

* Save your prompts, call scripts and knowledge-base text before you change anything.  
* Write down what the AI must do: answer, book, transfer, confirm and log to your CRM.  
* Try two options, and check each one’s trial or refund terms first.  
* Forward your existing number to the new tool and place test calls. You can port the number later.  
* If you take patient calls, get the BAA terms in writing for your plan.  
* Cancel Bland only after the new setup has handled real calls well.

**Which One Should You Try First?**

Each tool here offers a trial or free credit, so the most reliable way to decide is to forward your number to one and listen to how it handles your own callers. If you take patient calls, sign the BAA first and use made-up details until you have.

Of the tools here that don’t need a developer, Botphonic is the one I’d start with, because you pay for the minutes you use, the credit doesn’t expire, and you can try it on your own calls before you’re charged. Whichever tool you pick, listen to its sample or demo call and read its trial or refund terms before you move a number.

If Botphonic sounds right, you can [start the 14-day trial with 20 free minutes](https://botphonic.ai/pricing/).

## **FAQs**

1. **Does Bland have a warm transfer on its self-serve plans?**

Not on Start, Build, or Scale. See ‘What Bland’s Self-Serve Plans Include.

2. **Is Bland HIPAA compliant?**

Bland's pricing page lists a BAA for Enterprise only. Its FAQ lists several compliance frameworks, and I have not verified them either way. If you handle patient data, ask Bland for its documents and a signed BAA before you rely on it. I am not a lawyer, so this is not legal advice.

3. **What does Bland cost per minute, all in?**

There is no single number. The talk rate is \$0.14 on Start and \$0.12 on Build, and transfer time, outbound attempts, number fees, and phone service come on top. In my example above, 1,000 minutes comes to about \$143 on Start before number fees and phone service.

4. **Does Bland have texting on its self-serve plans?**

Not on Start or Build. Bland's SMS doc lists texting for Enterprise and Agent Phone, as of my October 2026 check.

5. **Can I keep my phone number when I switch?**

Often you can, by forwarding your existing number to the new tool first. Goodcall's pricing page, for example, says you can keep your number by forwarding it. Forwarding and porting differ by vendor, so ask each one, including Botphonic's team, what it supports.

6. **Do I have to tell callers they are speaking to an AI or being recorded?** 

Possibly. Recording-consent and AI-disclosure rules vary by state, so check your local requirements and ask the vendor what disclosure options it offers. Some states require all parties to consent to recording, so get consent up front if you serve callers in those states.
